clue.text: With ormolu hem, expensive coat need not be thrown away

indicators.note: a hem is the finishing edge of a garment, so only the word's final letter is wanted

blocks.note: the closing letter of the word
sable fur makes a famously costly coat

explanation.surface: A pricey fur coat with gilded trim is too good to throw out.
explanation.walkthrough: The coat seems to have an ormolu hem; really the hem is just the last letter of that word, set in front of the coat.
explanation.definitionFit: Something usable still serves a purpose, so there is no reason to discard it.

clue.text: James catches large fish

indicators.note: to catch something is to take hold of it, so the first name wraps around the next piece

blocks.note: Sid James, the Carry On comedy actor
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: An angler called James lands a big fish.
explanation.walkthrough: James here is a surname: the comic actor Sid James, star of the British Carry On films.
explanation.definitionFit: Sild are young herring, usually canned in Norway, so the word names a kind of fish.

clue.text: Dance supremo by a rising river

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means the word reads from bottom to top

blocks.note: the person in charge
taken as written
the River Avon, flowing through Stratford

explanation.surface: A dance led by the top person, beside a river in flood.
explanation.definitionFit: The bossa nova is a Brazilian style of music and the dance performed to it.

clue.text: Overhear organ piece that goes to the head

blocks.note: the organ of hearing

blocks.clueFragment: piece that goes to the head
blocks.note: a hairpiece worn on the head

explanation.surface: A musician overhears a passage of organ music that sticks in the head.
explanation.walkthrough: The organ piece looks like music; it is a body organ followed by a hairpiece.
explanation.definitionFit: To earwig is a British colloquial verb for eavesdropping on other people's conversation.

clue.text: Spike, having mangled cigar: 'Grand to go uncivilised!'

indicators.note: something mangled has been crushed out of shape, so the letters are rearranged
telling a letter it has to go means it is removed from the word

blocks.note: a barb is a sharp point
taken as written
G is the abbreviation for grand, a thousand

explanation.surface: Someone named Spike crushes a fine cigar and is told such behaviour is boorish.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove G from CIGAR before rearranging the remaining four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Barbaric describes savage, primitive conduct, the opposite of civilised behaviour.

clue.text: Understudy (being separated) to offer a bribe? Despicable!

blocks.note: split as under (beneath) and study (con, to examine closely)
a bribe is a temptation

explanation.surface: An understudy is accused of offering a bribe to get the part, which is shameful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Understudy' must be split into its two parts, as the parenthesis hints: under, then study.
explanation.definitionFit: Something despicable is so bad it does not even merit scorn, the sense of the idiom.

clue.text: Control keeps regressive creative activity in check

indicators.note: regressive means going backwards, so the word is read in reverse
to keep something is to hold it inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: to rein in is to control
the arts are creative pursuits

explanation.surface: Some form of control keeps backward-looking art in check.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Control' looks like the definition at the head of the clue; it is the outer piece, and the answer is defined by the last word.
explanation.definitionFit: To check something is to hold it back, the same as to restrain it.

clue.text: Upturned bar in an array

indicators.note: in a down entry, turned up means read from bottom to top
in places one piece inside another

blocks.note: a rod is a bar
taken as written

explanation.surface: An upended bar placed among a display of items.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Array' looks like a noun, a display; here it is the verb meaning to dress up.
explanation.definitionFit: To array is an old verb for decking or dressing finely, which is to decorate.

clue.text: Hesitant when cutting round tops of diseased elms

indicators.note: the tops of words in a down clue are their first letters
going round something means surrounding it

blocks.note: an incisive remark is a cutting one
initial letters of the two words

explanation.surface: A tree surgeon is reluctant to fell elms with Dutch elm disease.
explanation.definitionFit: An indecisive person cannot make up their mind and so hesitates.

clue.text: End career (very little in it)

blocks.note: a close is an end or conclusion
to career is to rush along, or run

explanation.surface: A career ends with hardly anything to show for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Career' is the verb meaning to rush, not a working life.
explanation.definitionFit: A close-run contest is one with a narrow margin between winner and loser.

clue.text: Inferior but did farrier work daily, no trouble

indicators.note: no says that something is absent, so those letters are taken out

blocks.note: a farrier fits horseshoes, so he shod the horse
taken as written
to ail is to trouble

explanation.surface: A blacksmith did shoddy work despite labouring hard every day with no problems.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove AIL from the middle of DAILY to leave DY.
explanation.definitionFit: Shoddy goods are badly made and of poor quality.

clue.text: Film technology from one involved with Iron Man cast

indicators.note: being involved means being tangled up, so all these letters are mixed together

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Special effects come from someone working with the Iron Man film cast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' looks like the anagram signal, but its letters belong to the fodder; the mixing is signalled by 'involved with'.
explanation.definitionFit: Animatronics is the use of electronically controlled puppets in film effects.

clue.text: Block one's put on a classical architectural feature

blocks.note: one is, I am, contracted to I'm
the triangular gable above a classical portico

explanation.surface: A block of stone is set on top of a Greek-style gable.
explanation.walkthrough: One's is read as one is, shortened to I'm.
explanation.definitionFit: An impediment is an obstruction, something that blocks progress.

clue.text: Shots, say, of parent going round topless

indicators.note: without its top, the word loses its first letter
turning round means facing the other way, so the word reads backwards

blocks.note: an American word for mother

explanation.surface: A mother runs around with no top on while photographs are taken.
explanation.walkthrough: Shots look like photographs; here they are bullets. Drop the first letter before turning the word round.
explanation.definitionFit: Ammo is short for ammunition, and shots are one example of it.

clue.text: Hot and stuffy — infuriated

blocks.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
a stuffy room lacks fresh air

explanation.surface: Someone stuck in a hot, stuffy room is getting furious.
explanation.walkthrough: Losing one's hair is British slang for losing one's temper, hence this sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Hairless is a British slang term for being furious, from the idiom of losing your hair in anger.

clue.text: Files possibly state: 'Mae West'

indicators.note: possibly suggests one of several arrangements of the letters

blocks.note: taken as written
to aver is to state firmly

explanation.surface: Documents quote the film star Mae West.
explanation.walkthrough: Mae West, the actress, gave her name to the inflatable life jacket used by RAF aircrew in WWII.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mae West is an inflatable life jacket, which is a device that saves lives at sea.

clue.text: Woody surrounding for work unit that produces a reaction?

indicators.note: surrounding something means enclosing it on all sides

blocks.note: Woody Allen, the film director
the erg is a unit of work in physics

explanation.surface: Wooden panelling around an office team provokes a response.
explanation.walkthrough: Woody is a first name here, the film-maker Woody Allen.
explanation.definitionFit: An allergen is any substance that triggers an allergic response in the body.

clue.text: Algiers revolves round harem?

indicators.note: revolving turns things about, so the letters change places

blocks.note: taken as written
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Is life in Algiers centred on a harem?
explanation.definitionFit: A seraglio is the women's quarters of an Ottoman palace, another word for a harem.

clue.text: One has to pursue female figure

blocks.note: F is the abbreviation for female
I have, contracted to I've

explanation.surface: Someone has to chase after a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: Since one has follows the female, the contraction comes second.
explanation.definitionFit: Five is a number, and a figure is a numeral.

clue.text: Son, mean and empty-headed

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for son
catty means spiteful or nasty

explanation.surface: A son described as spiteful and dim.
explanation.definitionFit: Scatty is British informal for scatterbrained, absent-minded and disorganised.

clue.text: Swindle associated with pieces of furniture? Rubbish!

blocks.note: a fiddle is a fraud or scam
sticks of furniture are individual items

explanation.surface: A scam involving furniture is dismissed as nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sticks of furniture' is an idiom for items of furniture, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Fiddlesticks is an old exclamation of impatience meaning nonsense.

clue.text: Decline fleshy fruit vociferously

indicators.note: vociferous means loudly voiced, so the word is heard rather than spelt

blocks.note: a drupe is a stone fruit with fleshy flesh, like a plum

explanation.surface: Someone loudly refuses a juicy piece of fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Decline' looks like refuse, but it means sink or sag.
explanation.definitionFit: To droop is to sag or sink downward, one sense of decline.

clue.text: Manner lacks latitude, causing a spot of discomfort

indicators.note: something that lacks a part is without it, so that letter is removed

blocks.note: style is a manner of doing things
L is the abbreviation for latitude

explanation.surface: A rigid manner with no flexibility causes some unease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A spot of discomfort' sounds like a little unease; it is literally a sore spot on the eyelid.
explanation.definitionFit: A stye is an inflamed swelling on the eyelid, a painful little spot.

clue.text: Take a lot of time to become affiliated

blocks.note: how long will it take is how long will it be
a long while

explanation.surface: It takes ages to be accepted into a group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take a lot of time' is BE LONG read as one word.
explanation.definitionFit: To belong is to be a member of a group, the state of having joined it.

clue.text: Prompt move to Vietnam, avoiding north

indicators.note: to move letters is to shift them into a new order
avoiding something means leaving it out

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
N is the abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: A sudden relocation to Vietnam, skipping the north of the country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Move' looks like part of the surface's relocation story; it signals the shuffle. 'Prompt' looks like an adjective but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To prompt someone is to spur them into action, which is to motivate them.

clue.text: Speed up undoing of nepotist

indicators.note: undoing something takes it apart, so the letters can be put back differently

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Hasten the downfall of someone who favours relatives.
explanation.definitionFit: Step on it is an idiom urging a driver to press the accelerator and go faster.

clue.text: Royal house about to return delivery

indicators.note: returning means going back the way it came, so the word reads backwards

blocks.note: the House of York, the medieval royal dynasty
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A royal household is about to send back a parcel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Delivery' looks like a parcel; it is a bowled ball in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: A yorker is a cricket ball bowled to land right at the batsman's feet, one type of delivery.
